capitals.name: Kodiak
capitals.note: Russia's first permanent settlement in Alaska was at Three Saints Bay on Kodiak Island (1784); the page says only that the colonial headquarters were 'moved from Kodiak' in 1808, so the years before are the researcher's reading. Coordinates are the researcher's.

capitals.name: New Archangel (Sitka)
capitals.note: 'In 1808, Redoubt Saint Michael was rebuilt as New Archangel and became the capital of Russian America'; a timeline entry gives 1804. Coordinates are the researcher's.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1784, ... founded Russia's first permanent settlement in Alaska at Three Saints Bay' on Kodiak Island; the page gives no extent beyond the settlement, so only Kodiak is drawn. Soft.

correction.text: Alaska, the Russian America of 1867: 'the United States had grown by 586,412 sq mi (1,518,800 km2)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Russian colonial possessions in the Americas were collectively known as Russian America from 1799 to 1867', held by the Russian-American Company; the 1824 treaty 'recognized exclusive Russian rights to the fur trade north of latitude 54 40 N' and the 1825 convention ran the panhandle border 10 marine leagues (56 km) inland to the 141st meridian west and north to the Frozen Ocean. Sanity check: the Alaska Purchase page gives 1,518,800 km2; the gazetteer's Alaska is 1.57 M km2 (ratio 1.04). The outline is Alaska as it was sold; before 1825 the claim was vaguer (soft). Fort Ross (1812-1841) and Fort Elizabeth (1814-1817) are drawn by ledger events as outliers, not in the keyframe.

region.text: Kodiak Island and Three Saints Bay, Russia's first permanent settlement in Alaska

ledger.note: 1784: Russia's first permanent settlement in Alaska. 'In 1784, ... founded Russia's first permanent settlement in Alaska at Three Saints Bay', on Kodiak Island. The page also says 'From 1732 to 1867, the Russian Empire laid claim to northern Pacific Coast territories in the Americas'.

region.text: Alaska, the Russian America of 1867: 'the United States had grown by 586,412 sq mi (1,518,800 km2)'

ledger.note: 1799: the Russian-American Company and the name Russian America. 'Rezanov formed the Russian-American Company' in 1799 and 'Russian colonial possessions in the Americas were collectively known as Russian America from 1799 to 1867'; the page gives no boundary for 1799, so the whole of present Alaska stands for the claim (Alaska is the gazetteer's alias for Russian America).

1808: New Archangel becomes the capital. 'In 1808, Redoubt Saint Michael was rebuilt as New Archangel and became the capital of Russian America after the previous colonial headquarters were moved from Kodiak.' A timeline entry on the same page dates Novo-Arkhangelsk (Sitka) to 1804.
1812: Fort Ross in California. 'From 1812 to 1841, the Russians operated Fort Ross, California.' The page does not mention the Spanish claim to California; the land is read as held by no state.

region.text: Fort Elizabeth on Kauai, Kingdom of Hawaii

ledger.note: 1814: Fort Elizabeth on Kauai. 'From 1814 to 1817, Russian Fort Elizabeth was operating in the Kingdom of Hawaii.'

region.text: Fort Elizabeth on Kauai, Kingdom of Hawaii

ledger.note: 1817: the Russians leave Fort Elizabeth ('From 1814 to 1817').

region.text: the mainland coastal strip of the Alaska panhandle south of Cape Spencer, leased to the Hudson's Bay Company (the researcher's approximation of the strip)

ledger.note: 1839: the panhandle is leased to the Hudson's Bay Company. 'The British Hudson's Bay Company was leased the southern edge of Russian America in 1839 under the RAC-HBC Agreement'; the 1825 convention page puts the leased land as the mainland coast 'south of Cape Spencer' after the 1834 Dryad affair.
1841: Fort Ross ends. 'From 1812 to 1841, the Russians operated Fort Ross, California'; the page does not say who took over.

region.text: the mainland coastal strip of the Alaska panhandle south of Cape Spencer, leased to the Hudson's Bay Company (the researcher's approximation of the strip)

ledger.note: 1867: the lease ends with the sale. Neither page gives the end or renewals of the 1839 lease; the researcher ends it with the transfer of the colony on 18 October 1867 (confidence 1, bridging).

region.text: Alaska, the Russian America of 1867: 'the United States had grown by 586,412 sq mi (1,518,800 km2)'

ledger.note: 1867: Alaska passes to the United States. 'The negotiations concluded ... with the signing of the treaty at 04:00 on March 30, 1867'; 'The transfer ceremony took place in Sitka on October 18, 1867'; price $7.2 million for 586,412 sq mi (1,518,800 km2). The Russian America page has the payment on April 9, 1867 and the Alaska Purchase page the Senate ratification on May 15 (the pages differ).

region.text: Alaska, the Russian America of 1867: 'the United States had grown by 586,412 sq mi (1,518,800 km2)'

ledger.note: 1867: Russian America ends at the Sitka ceremony of 18 October 1867.

certainty.note: A claim to the northern Pacific coast with a few settlements and no treaty boundary.

The eastern and southern borders with British North America are sharp from the Anglo-Russian Convention of 28 February 1825 (panhandle 10 marine leagues inland, 141st meridian west to the Arctic Ocean); the interior and the Aleutian chain stay soft.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row (Cliopatria folds Alaska into its Russian Empire shapes, whose Alaska cells the east-Europe/Siberia group should check against this dossier). Three pages opened: Russian America, Alaska Purchase, Anglo-Russian Convention of 1825 (budget 2-5). Not on the pages: the extent of the Russian claim before 1825 (the Ukase of 1821), the infobox area (garbled on the extract), Russian posts other than Kodiak, Sitka, Fort Ross and Fort Elizabeth, the end of the 1839 lease, the Russo-American Treaty of 1824 beyond its one sentence, any war with the Tlingit. Disagreements: Sitka 1804 (timeline) vs 1808 (text); the Senate vote and payment dates (Russian America page: payment 9 April 1867; Alaska Purchase page: ratified 15 May 1867); the Anglo-Russian convention date 28 February 1825 (new style) is the only date on the page. The vassal events are a modelling choice: a lease of the coastal strip to the HBC (counterpart rupert-s-land, written in this batch). The settlement dates and the 1732 claim start: the page says 'From 1732 to 1867, the Russian Empire laid claim'; the dossier starts at the 1784 settlement.
